s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status and respiratory acidosis in a post-surgical patient with multiple comorbidities
salient_findings: Severe metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap
key_facts: 75-year-old woman with a prosthetic hip infection
Recent revision surgery
Chronic kidney disease with baseline creatinine 130-150 μmol/L
Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Home medications included aspirin, bisoprolol, atorvastatin, furosemide, and others
Developed symptoms on hospital day 10
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12
Temperature 36.2°C, blood pressure 145/66 mmHg, pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min
Arterial blood gas showed pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess -22.7 mmol/L
Corrected anion gap was 25 mmol/L
Lactic acid 0.7 mmol/L, blood ketones <0.2 mmol/L, salicylate <0.4 mmol/L

shortlist.label: Lactic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anion gap and metabolic acidosis

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Post-surgical patient with prosthetic hip infection and altered mental status

shortlist.label: Uremic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic kidney disease and elevated creatinine

shortlist.label: Respiratory failure
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperventilation and abnormal arterial blood gas

shortlist.label: Vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity
shortlist.why_kept: Recent vancomycin use and potential kidney injury

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a prosthetic hip infection, recent revision surgery, and development of symptoms such as drowsiness, confusion, and hyperventilation on hospital day 10, along with laboratory findings including a high neutrophil count and metabolic acidosis, are most consistent with sepsis.

rejected.label: Lactic acidosis
rejected.why: Lactic acid level was normal at 0.7 mmol/L

rejected.label: Uremic acidosis
rejected.why: Renal function was unchanged and insufficient to explain the degree of acidosis

rejected.label: Respiratory failure
rejected.why: Oxygen saturation was 99% on room air, indicating no respiratory failure

rejected.label: Vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity
rejected.why: There was no evidence of worsening renal function to suggest vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity
